(1) the addition of the thiol diluent MCU to the DNA layer on gold improves the hybridization efficiency of the DNA layer and (2) the presence of nonspecific proteins from serum dilutions reduces the hybridization efficiency and the kinetics of DNA hybridization on the DNA layer.

the development and characterization of mixed adlayer systems on metal surfaces for nucleic acid assays from a complex milieu.
the development of a new approach for the direct assay of nucleic acids from a complex biological environment using SPR.
developing new methods for nucleic acid assays that are simple, rapid, sensitive, and robust, and can be performed directly from biological fluids and other complex media.

MCU addition into DNA adlayers improves both DNA capture and hybridized signal from serum dilutions.

the addition of MCU to DNA probe layers on gold surfaces enhances DNA hybridization performance and improves surface resistance to both protein adsorption and nonspecific DNA adsorption from a serum milieu.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mixed DNA/MCU monolayer adlayers on gold provide an effective surface for DNA hybridization from complex biological milieu.

mixed DNA/MCU monolayers on Au provide optimal DNA capture from serum dilutions and that SPR provides a sensitive and quantitative method for the study of nucleic acid hybridization from complex biological milieus.

mixed DNA/mercaptoalkanol adlayers on gold are promising platforms for nucleic acid assay from complex milieu, but further research and development is required to optimize the assay performance and to address nonspecific protein adsorptions from the sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a mixed DNA/MCU monolayer on gold is an attractive platform for nucleic acid assay from biological samples.
mixed DNA/mercaptoalkanethiol adlayers on gold provide a simple, robust, and inexpensive platform for DNA detection from complex biological milieus.
the use of mixed DNA/MCU monolayers on a solid support can provide an attractive approach for nucleic acid capture and detection from complex biological media.
